title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'Kummer' Galois representation attached to a homomorphism of abelian groups ξ (here written j): A → G_m(S) = Γ(S,O_S^*), where S is a connected scheme in characteristic 0 with geometric point s̄. Extracting all n-th roots of the units j(a) gives a pro-étale torsor E_∞(j)_S under Hom_Z(A,T), with T = Ẑ(1) = lim μ_n. Its automorphism group G_j sits in an extension 1 → Hom_Z(A,T) → G_j → Ẑ^* (in fact Hom(A,T) ⋊ Ẑ^*). The fundamental group acts through a homomorphism ρ_j = γ_j: π_1(S,s̄) → G_j that lies over the cyclotomic character.

On the previous page he proved functoriality in A: an arrow A' → A induces G_j → G_{j'}, compatible with the representations. On this page he concludes that, to study the image of γ_j, one may assume j is injective (350). In that case A can be replaced by its image A/ker j in G_m(S).

He then 'divides' the diagram further. He sets π_1^+ = Ker(χ_π: π_1 → Ẑ^*), the kernel of the cyclotomic character (351). This gives a morphism of exact sequences (352): π_1^+ → Hom_Z(A,T), π_1 → G_j, and the identity on Ẑ^*. Writing π̃_1 = Im γ_j, π̃_1^+ = Im γ_j^+ and Γ = Im χ_π (353), one gets an exact sequence 1 → π̃_1^+ → π̃_1 → Γ → 1 (354). So the 'size' of the Kummer image reduces to two pieces: the size of the cyclotomic image Γ, and the size of the image of the 'geometric/cyclotomic-trivial' part in Hom(A,T).

The next page sets up the expected theorem. For A finitely generated, S of finite type over Q and normal, and j injective, Γ is open in Ẑ^*, and the aim is to show that π̃_1^+ is open in Hom(A,Ẑ(1)), presumably after dividing out torsion. This is the openness of the Kummer image for G_m (Bashmakov/Ribet-type Kummer theory), reduced to the generic point of S.
errors: He refers to 'diviser encore un peu le diagramme (348)'; (348) is the composite A' → A → G_m(S). The diagram meant is (349), or perhaps (346). This is a numbering slip.
No mathematical error. Exactness of (354) holds because the right-hand vertical map in (352) is the identity, so Ker(π̃_1 → Γ) = γ_j(π_1^+).

Implicit gap: for openness in Hom(A,T) one must also handle torsion in A, i.e. roots of unity in j(A). This is not addressed on this page; the next page lists conditions but does not visibly treat torsion.

ideas.what: Kummer torsor/representation attached to j: A → G_m(S), with values in Hom(A,Ẑ(1)) ⋊ Ẑ^*
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory / Kummer representation of a 1-motive [A → G_m]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; 1-motive formulation by Deligne (Hodge III, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the Kummer/Galois-action discussions in La Longue Marche (1981); not verified

ideas.what: Reduction to j injective by functoriality in A
Splitting the image into the cyclotomic image Γ and the image of the kernel of the cyclotomic character in Hom(A,T)
ideas.modern_name: Image of Galois over K(μ_∞): the Kummer part Gal(K(μ_∞, A^{1/∞})/K(μ_∞))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bashmakov, Ribet (1979, Kummer theory on extensions of abelian varieties by tori)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine dévissage in the Kummer theory of G_m. The target result (open image in Hom(A,Ẑ(1)) for finitely generated A in fields of finite type over Q) is classical, due to Bashmakov, Ribet and others.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out line reads 'Je suppose désormais' rather than 'Je suppose dirons'.
In (350) the target is G_m(S); it is written like 'Gm(S)'.

The garbled sentence should read roughly: 'On peut considérer l'étude de la "taille" de Im(γ_j: π_1 → G_j) comme essentiellement ramenée à celle de la taille de Im χ_π et de celle de Im γ_j^+ ; de façon précise, si on pose'.
